assessment: Used-data numerical reproduction, not independent validation or an engine effect
geography: NIH Clinical Center, Bethesda, Maryland, United States
limitations: This is a contrast between whole offered menu regimens in a short inpatient crossover, not an isolated processing or ingredient effect.
No washout separates the diets; an order/period sensitivity does not prove absence of carryover.
The archive is the author's derived daily-intake table, not a new audit of meal records or original measurement systems.
Meal-specific macronutrients, body-composition adjustments and all other endpoints are outside this reproduction.
No conversion from kcal/day to a continuous UPF dose, diabetes hazard, mortality or healthspan is identified. The engine and scientific-release blockers remain unchanged.

Participant-level sampling intervals under the stated model; no national transport, food-category dose response, dietary hazard, mortality, missingness, measurement-error or carryover uncertainty is claimed to be resolved.
population: Twenty adult inpatient volunteers; paired offered-menu contrast, not a national cohort

corrections.assessment: The accessible PMC notice describes a meal-level diet-order error and states that the primary total-daily-intake endpoint was unaffected.

PubMed verifies the separate erratum. Publisher body was unavailable during intake; Hall's January 21, 2021 response associates it with the meal-label correction. Preserve both identifiers; do not infer a different daily-intake adjustment from their inconsistent chronology.

source.citation: Hall KD et al. Cell Metabolism. 2019;30(1):67-77.e3. Author OSF ADLDataSAScode2.zip, uploaded January 28, 2021, version 1.
source.correction_note: Both errata retained in the reproduction protocol: 10.1016/j.cmet.2019.05.020 and 10.1016/j.cmet.2020.08.014. Accessible PMC notice says total daily intake is unaffected by the meal-label correction. Author archive uploaded after January 2021 correction discussion; body-composition and meal-level endpoints excluded.

period_sensitivity.design: paired difference = diet_contrast + common_period_effect * (+1 PROC second, -1 PROC first)
period_sensitivity.limitation: Additive common period assumption; differential carryover is not identified

time_period: 2018 trial; two consecutive 14-day diet periods; author archive January 2021
